Previous lessons:
Navigation copy changes on home intro and list layout redesigns for friend selection were helpful, achieving statistically significant wins.
Reordering sign-in to after friend selection, split-screen companion persona selectors, and background desktop alerts significantly worsened performance.
Hints, wait time indicators, new screens, new activity flows, redesign layouts, and incentives showed no clear effect.
Predictions were too high for sign-in reordering, split-screen persona selectors, desktop alerts, and early guide screens.
Predictions were too low for navigation copy improvements and list layout redesigns, which resulted in strong wins despite neutral or negative initial predictions.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Navigation copy changes on home intro and list layout redesigns for friend selection were helpful, achieving statistically significant wins.
Reordering sign-in to after friend selection, split-screen companion persona selectors, and background desktop alerts significantly worsened performance.
Hints, wait time indicators, new screens, new activity flows, non-list layout redesigns, and incentives showed no clear effect.
Predictions were too high for sign-in reordering, split-screen persona selectors, background desktop alerts, and early guide screens.
Predictions were too low for navigation copy improvements on home intro and list layout redesigns for friend selection.
